subject.title: Feature: Reason-aware cron guardrails (quota/auth/rate-limit aware backoff + circuit breaker)

question: What default recurring cron guard policy should OpenClaw own for billing, auth/auth_permanent, format, rate_limit, and unknown errors, and which persisted state/config/protocol/UI surfaces should expose it?
rationale: The remaining work changes compatibility-sensitive cron defaults, persisted state, public protocol/UI visibility, and provider/auth cooldown semantics, which automation cannot choose safely without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve coordinated guard layer
options.body: Define one reason-aware recurring cron policy with explicit state, protocol, docs, tests, compatibility-safe defaults, and provider/auth cooldown coordination.

options.title: Split by failure class
options.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella but require separate sponsored work for billing, auth, rate-limit, and UI/state visibility decisions.

options.title: Defer core policy
options.body: Leave generic recurring backoff in place and accept only narrow opt-in PRs until stronger live evidence or product direction exists.

recommendation.title: Approve coordinated guard layer
recommendation.body: Define one reason-aware recurring cron policy with explicit state, protocol, docs, tests, compatibility-safe defaults, and provider/auth cooldown coordination.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete provided the prior keep-open review and has adjacent recurring cron retry history, making them the best available routing owner for the policy choice.
